feature: The pill under a drag says the key and the time on a keyed layer
summary: While you drag, resize or turn a layer that has keys, the pill under it now reads a diamond and the playhead time before the size, so you can see where the change lands without looking down at the strip. A layer with no keys reads exactly as before.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: a-keyed-drag-says-the-key-and-the-time-walk (picture) and a-keyed-drag-on-a-video-says-the-key-and-the-time-walk (video).

try.do: New picture, draw a rectangle, pick it, and pull its bottom right corner: the pill says only the size.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press K (Add Key), then click 1s on the strip's ruler.
Drag the rectangle and hold: the pill says the diamond, 0:01.00, then its size.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pull a corner and hold: the diamond, the time, then the size.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the round turn knob above the layer and hold: the diamond, the time, the size and the turn.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: On a video, add a title at 1 second, press Add Key, and drag the title: the same pill.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does the diamond and time at the front of the pill tell you the change is about to key, without a glance at the strip?
Is hundredths of a second (0:01.00) the right precision under the hand, even on a video whose transport says 0:01?
On a keyed layer a move reads the size rather than where it is going, as the mock draws it. Do you miss the position while moving?
Does the pill stay out of the way of a corner swung down by a turn?
rough: Matches the mock: on a keyed layer the pill reads the size for a move, a resize and a turn alike. A layer with no keys keeps today's readings (a move says where it is going, a turn says nothing), so the same move reads differently once the layer has keys.
A whole selection moved at once, a copy dragged off with Option, a path point and a corner radius drag keep their plain readings; only one layer in the hand says where its own key lands.
With the transform values popover open, a move, a resize and a turn are read there and no pill shows, keyed or not, as before.
